body:
### Summary

### Problem Statement

Python's packaging spec doesn't define a way to specify that a project is compatible only with a particular operating system. Developers can use the `project.classifiers` field to define compatible operating systems, but that is informational-only, not a firm requirement for installers to abide by.

As a result, uv errors if you have a workspace with the following members:

```toml
[project]
name = "a"
classifiers = [ "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows" ]
dependencies = [ "numpy==1" ]
```

```toml
[project]
name = "b"
classifiers = [ "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux" ]
dependencies = [ "numpy==2" ]
```

The user never intends to install these two members at the same time, but since uv doesn't know that, `uv sync --all-packages` errors. The most robust solution to this issue is to explicitly pin an environment for each dependency, for example:

```toml
[project]
name = "a"
classifiers = [ "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows" ]
dependencies = [ "numpy==1; platform_system=='Windows'" ]
```

```toml
[project]
name = "b"
classifiers = [ "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux" ]
dependencies = [ "numpy==2; platform_system=='Linux'" ]
```

There are a couple issues with this approach:
* It's redundant. The compatible platform is already listed in the classifier.
* It's excessively verbose. If you have hundreds of dependencies, it's gross to need to add "platform_system=='Windows'" to all of them.
* It's not strict. uv will still attempt to install the member, even if it skips installing all of its dependencies.

### Proposed Solution

Add a `supported-environments` setting to uv. Developers can specify supported environments in each member's pyproject.toml.

Example:

```toml
[project]
name = "a"
classifiers = [ "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows" ]
dependencies = [ "numpy==1" ]

[tool.uv]
supported-environments = [ "platform_system=='Windows'" ]
```

```toml
[project]
name = "b"
classifiers = [ "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux" ]
dependencies = [ "numpy==2" ]

[tool.uv]
supported-environments = [ "platform_system=='Linux'" ]
```

The available environment markers and semantics are the exact same ones uv currently respects for dependencies: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/c4e9150bc11eb29ae8f366430332b9592b9f9044/crates/uv-pep508/src/marker/environment.rs#L18-L30.

Misc. notes:
* if `supported-environments` is not specified, uv behaves the same way it currently does
* running `uv sync --package` on a project with an incompatible environment gives a helpful error message
* running `uv sync --all-packages` syncs all projects with compatible environments

### Alternatives I Considered

* Going off of `classifiers` directly.
    * `classifiers` doesn't actually have a firm definition. It also feels directionally incorrect to have two distinct ways of defining environments. It would be nice if we could reuse the exact same environment markers and semantics as dependencies.
* Reusing the existing `tool.uv.environments` field in members' pyproject.tomls.
    * These usages seem related but distinct, so I suggest a distinct field `supported-environments`.

### Example

I would be happy to implement this as well!
title: Support per-project environment constraints for workspace dependency resolution
